Signal track

Source: R/geom-ridge-track.R
geom_ridge_track.Rd

Draws a quantitative signal over genomic ranges, such as ChIP-seq coverage, a bedGraph, or GISTIC scores, as a shaded area under a step curve. Each range is drawn flat at its value from start to end. Ranges further apart than max_gap are not joined, so missing data is left blank.

There are two modes, set by the mapping:

  • Overlay: map the signal to y to draw curves on a shared continuous axis, e.g. aes(y = score, fill = group). The area is shaded between 0 and the signal.

  • Ridges: map a discrete variable to y and the signal to height to draw one curve per row, e.g. aes(y = sample, height = signal). Heights are scaled so the largest absolute value spans ridge_scale rows.

xmin and xmax default to the start and end columns. For single position data, map x instead, e.g. aes(x = position, y = signal), and the points are joined directly.

Usage

geom_ridge_track(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  ridge_scale = 0.9,
  max_gap = 1,
  outline.type = "upper",
  ...,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping

Set of aesthetic mappings created by ggplot2::aes().

data

GRanges object or data frame of ranges with seqnames, start, and end columns plus one or more signal columns, in long format with one row per range and group.

ridge_scale

In ridge mode, the height of the largest absolute signal in rows, default: 0.9. Values above 1 let ridges overlap.

max_gap

Largest distance in bp between the end of one range and the start of the next for the two to be joined, default: 1. Use Inf to always join.

outline.type

Which sides of the area to outline when colour is set, one of "upper", "lower", "both", or "full". See ggplot2::geom_ribbon().

...

Other arguments passed to ggplot2::layer(), e.g. colour, fill, alpha, or linewidth.

na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

See ggplot2::layer().

Value

ggplot2 layer

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# GISTIC scores, deletions drawn below zero; segments are ~10 kb apart so join them
gistic <- data.table::fread("scores.gistic", check.names = TRUE)
gistic <- gistic[, .(seqnames = Chromosome, start = Start, end = End, Type,
                     G.score = ifelse(Type == "Del", -G.score, G.score))]

ggplot2::ggplot(gistic) +
  geom_ridge_track(ggplot2::aes(y = G.score, fill = Type, group = Type), max_gap = 1e5) +
  coord_locus("chr13:48303751-48481890", flank = 1e6) +
  theme_genomic()

# ChIP-seq signal, one ridge per sample
chip <- devgru::read_bed_file("signal.bedGraph", additional_col_names = c("sample", "signal"))

ggplot2::ggplot(chip) +
  geom_ridge_track(ggplot2::aes(y = sample, height = signal, fill = sample)) +
  coord_locus("chr1:203200001-203893000") +
  theme_genomic()
} # }
